citations.quote: Let $X$ be a closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold and let $P\to X$ be a smooth principal $SU(2)$-bundle with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. The Hodge star on two-forms is $*$, and $F_A^-=(F_A-*F_A)/2$ denotes the anti-self-dual projection of the curvature of a connection $A$. The equation used in this item is $F_A^-=0$, so the curvature is self-dual; this convention and the negative second Chern number are fixed together for the positive-definite orientation. The self-dual moduli set is the set of smooth connections satisfying $F_A^-=0$, modulo the action of smooth gauge transformations of $P$. At a solution, the deformation complex is $0\to\Omega^0(X;\operatorname{ad}P)\xrightarrow{d_A}\Omega^1(X;\operatorname{ad}P)\xrightarrow{d_A^-}\Omega^-(X;\operatorname{ad}P)\to0$, and its gauge-fixed operator is $D_A=d_A^*\oplus d_A^-$. For index calculations, $D_A$ is completed from the first Sobolev space of one-forms to the direct sum of the zeroth Sobolev spaces of zero-forms and anti-self-dual two-forms.

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed simply connected oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold with positive-definite intersection form, and $E$ a Hermitian rank-two bundle with fixed unit determinant and $c_2(E)[X]=-1$. Use the equation $F_A^-=0$ and the unbased $H^3/H^4$ configuration quotient. The actual smooth reducible solution orbits are finite. Sending such a solution to its pair of parallel eigenlines gives an injection into the unordered pairs $\{x,-x\}$ in $H^2(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $x^2[X]=1$. Distinct pairs arising in this way are orthogonal, so there are at most $b_2(X)$ reducible solution orbits.

At each such orbit there are invariant Coulomb-slice coordinates with effective circle stabilizer. The finite obstruction map is a smooth circle-equivariant map $\phi:\mathbb C^{3+p}\to\mathbb C^p$, with $\phi(0)=D\phi(0)=0$ and scalar circle action of the same nonzero weight on both spaces. Arbitrarily small $C^1(H^3,H^2)$, bounded $H^3$-valued, equivariant perturbations supported near that orbit can be chosen so that their zero set near it, before taking the circle quotient, is equivariantly diffeomorphic to a neighborhood of $0$ in $\mathbb C^3$. After quotient it is a cone on $\mathbb{CP}^2$, with smooth irreducible punctured part. The finitely many constructions may have disjoint supports.

Deleting a smaller cone neighborhood leaves a smooth boundary link diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$. An orientation of the surrounding regular moduli manifold induces one of its two orientations; the result does not assert a common sign for distinct links. This is a local preparation operation and does not assert a small-instanton end or a global compactification.

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed simply connected oriented Riemannian four-manifold with positive-definite intersection form, and let $P\to X$ be an $SU(2)$-bundle with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. Complete the connections in $H^3$ and the gauge transformations in $H^4$, and use the unbased irreducible configuration quotient. The curvature section $\Phi([A])=F_A^-$ takes values in its $H^2$ equation bundle. Choose an open subset $U$ covered by finitely many bounded Coulomb slice balls centered at smooth irreducible connections, and an open $V$ whose closure is contained in the union of strictly smaller closed balls in these charts, their images lying in $U$.

Allow smooth gauge-equivariant perturbation sections supported in $U$, whose slice representatives are smooth $H^3$-valued maps with finite uniform $H^3$ norm on the specified chart balls. Interpret them in the $H^2$ equation bundle by inclusion. Give this class the topology of the uniform $H^3$ section norm on those finitely many balls together with convergence of the section and its slice derivative $H^3\to H^2$ uniformly on compact subsets. The perturbations for which $\Phi+\sigma$ is transverse to zero at every zero in $\overline V$ form an open dense subset. Their zero sets in $V$ are smooth orientable five-manifolds, and the real determinant line of the gauge-fixed deformation family is orientable on the irreducible quotient. The based quotient may be used to pull back this orientation; it carries an additional $SO(3)$ framing fiber and is not the unbased five-dimensional moduli space.

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed oriented Riemannian four-manifold, let $P$ be a fixed principal $SU(2)$-bundle with charge $k=-\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$, and let $(A_j)$ be smooth connections satisfying $F_{A_j}^-=0$ and $\sup_j\int_X|F_{A_j}|^2\,d\mathrm{vol}<\infty$. Then a subsequence, bundle isomorphisms, and a finite set $S\subset X$ exist such that the transported connections converge in local Sobolev gauge on compact subsets of $X\setminus S$ to a self-dual connection on a possibly lower-charge bundle of charge $k_\infty$. For each $p\in S$ there is a positive integer bubble charge $m_p$, and $k=k_\infty+\sum_{p\in S}m_p$. The limiting connection extends smoothly across every puncture after gauge transformation, and the compactified moduli space is obtained by adjoining the lower-charge limits together with the finite bubble points and their integer charge labels.

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed connected simply connected oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold with positive-definite intersection form, and fix a smooth $SU(2)$ bundle $P$ with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. The unperturbed self-dual moduli space has a neighborhood of its ideal stratum consisting precisely of the flat connection and one charge-one point, and this neighborhood, including the ideal stratum, is diffeomorphic in its interior and homeomorphic up to that stratum to $X\times[0,\lambda_0)$. Its interior consists of irreducible regular solutions. The parameter on the second factor is a smooth positive concentration scale tending to zero at the ideal stratum. Every sufficiently concentrating solution occurs, and occurs once. In particular this is a complete end theorem, not merely existence of a five-parameter family. It does not assert that arbitrary perturbations preserve this end.

Assume full AC. Let $P$ be a smooth principal $SU(2)$-bundle over a connected closed Riemannian four-manifold $X$. Fix a smooth reference connection and use the corresponding finite-chart Sobolev norms. Let $\mathcal A^3$ be its affine $H^3$ space of connections, and let $\mathcal G^4$ be the group of $H^4$ sections of the bundle with fiber $SU(2)$ and conjugation transition maps. A connection is called irreducible when its stabilizer in this group is precisely the two constant central transformations. The irreducible locus is open. Its quotient $\mathcal B^*=\mathcal A^{3,*}/(\mathcal G^4/\{\pm1\})$ is a Hausdorff, second-countable smooth Hilbert manifold. At each irreducible $A$, a neighborhood is represented uniquely by a sufficiently small ball in $\ker(d_A^*:H^3(\Lambda^1\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^2(\operatorname{ad}P))$.

The corresponding quotient of $H^2(\Lambda^-\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ is a smooth Hilbert bundle over $\mathcal B^*$, with smooth curvature section $[A]\mapsto F_A^-$. Its slice linearization is $a\mapsto d_A^-a$. Fixing a point of $P$ above $x_0\in X$, quotienting instead by transformations with value $1$ there gives a principal $SO(3)$-bundle over $\mathcal B^*$. In local product coordinates the curvature section is its pullback. In particular its linearization has three additional kernel directions and the same cokernel; framing must not be identified with the unbased deformation problem.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$. There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **Prepare precisely the actual reducibles.** Apply [F2] to their finite set and choose disjoint bounded invariant slice neighborhoods. Its constructed smoothing section $\sigma_r$ is supported in their union and vanishes at the central reducible points. On smaller neighborhoods its zeros are equivariant smooth graphs over $\mathbb C^3$; the punctured quotients are smooth oriented five-manifolds, and cutting their graph-radius gives projective links. There are no additional reducible solutions inside these slice neighborhoods: the stabilizer of a nearby orbit is a subgroup of the center's circle by the local slice construction; a reducible orbit must therefore be fixed by that circle. On its fixed diagonal subspace the equivariant off-diagonal perturbation is zero. The diagonal equation is the abelian self-dual equation, whose only local slice solution is the center because its $H^1$ is zero. Outside these neighborhoods the equation remains unperturbed, so [F2] lists all remaining reducibles. The construction is bounded and smooth into $H^3$ in these finitely many slices.

**Compactness for this prepared equation and a genuine middle region.** The supports in step 1.1 are in bounded $H^3$ slice balls. For a zero in such a ball the equation $d_{A_i}^-a=-F_{A_i}^--(a\wedge a)^--\sigma_r(a)$ has bounded $H^3$ right side, since $H^3$ is an algebra and the section is uniformly $H^3$ bounded. Together with $d_{A_i}^*a=0$, the Green estimate [F5] bounds $a$ in $H^4$. Thus zeros there have compact $H^3$ closure, including along the edges of the support. Any sequence of zeros outside these balls is unperturbed, so [F4] supplies its smooth or ideal subsequence. The bounded balls cannot approach an ideal point: their curvature has a uniform $L^4$ bound from the $H^3$ bound, so its energy on a ball of volume tending to zero tends uniformly to zero by Holder. Therefore a sufficiently small whole ideal collar from [F4] misses all the supports. The prepared equation is literally unperturbed there, retaining its entire regular end. Delete a smaller portion of that collar and smaller reducible cone neighborhoods. The remaining zero set is compact and irreducible, by the two sequence arguments just given. Cover this compact set by finitely many bounded irreducible Coulomb-slice collars, avoiding the protected smaller end and cone neighborhoods, and choose larger/smaller radii as in [F3].

**Relative middle transversality with all ends preserved.** Apply the finite-dimensional cokernel-direction and Sard proof of [F3] to $\Phi+\sigma_r$ on these middle collars, multiplying its new directions by bumps supported there. The fixed $\sigma_r$ is allowed in those charts: transition gauges on bounded chart sets have uniform $H^4$ bounds, and its original finite smooth target vectors and coordinate cutoffs consequently have uniformly bounded $H^3$ representatives. The derivative is a compact perturbation of the original Fredholm slice derivative, so its index remains five. The actual compact zero-container in [F3] and its positive-minimum argument exclude all new middle zeros outside the chosen smaller covering neighborhoods when the finite parameters are small. Around the protected cone and ideal collars the equation and its regularity remain exactly as in steps 1.1–2.1; on the compact transition overlaps, openness of surjectivity preserves their regularity. Thus a sufficiently small regular finite parameter makes every irreducible zero transverse. The same proof gives openness and density for all further allowed small middle sections. Both perturbations are zero outside the finite original and middle slice neighborhoods. For every resulting zero sequence in their union the same bounded-section $H^4$ estimate gives a converging $H^3$ subsequence; outside their union [F4] applies unchanged. This proves compactness of the full ideal completion and excludes any other ends, without applying an unperturbed compactness theorem to a nonzero perturbation.

**The actual smooth cut bordism.** The determinant line orients the transverse irreducible zero set by [F3], and its compact-derivative homotopy includes the fixed reducible preparation. At the ideal stratum, [F4]'s actual center-scale diffeomorphism and homeomorphic ideal extension provide a smooth collar $X\times[0,\lambda_0)$. At each reducible, [F2]'s graph-radius coordinate gives the smooth punctured cone collar $(0,\delta)\times\mathbb{CP}^2$. Delete its part of radius less than a smaller positive number. These finitely many collars are disjoint from each other and from the ideal collar. Step 3.1 makes the remaining interior compact up to the displayed collars, so the cut completion is a compact smooth five-manifold with exactly those boundary components. The induced boundary orientation on each projective link is its complex orientation or its negative. On the unique component meeting the connected ideal boundary choose the determinant orientation's global sign so this boundary orientation agrees with the given orientation of $X$; arbitrary other components cause no additional boundary strata. The number of links is exactly the number of actual reducibles, bounded by [F2]. This proves the compatible perturbation, compactified-strata and smooth cut-bordism assertions.

citations.quote: Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold. Its integral intersection lattice is the abelian group $L_X=H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$ with the integer-valued symmetric bilinear pairing $Q_X(\bar x,\bar y)=\langle \operatorname{PD}^{-1}(x)\smile\operatorname{PD}^{-1}(y),[X]\rangle$. Here $\operatorname{Tor}$ is the subgroup of elements of finite order, $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation class, and $\operatorname{PD}:H^2(X;\mathbb Z)\to H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the Poincaré duality isomorphism. The rank is $b_2(X)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_2(X;\mathbb Q)$. The lattice is positive definite when $Q_X(x,x)>0$ for every nonzero $x\in L_X$; it is unimodular when a Gram matrix in an integral basis has determinant $1$ or $-1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold with $\pi_1(X)=0$. Its integral intersection lattice on $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$ is a finite-rank free abelian group and its intersection pairing is unimodular.

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed simply connected oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold with positive-definite intersection form, and let $P\to X$ be an $SU(2)$ bundle with $c_2(P)[X]=-1$. Use the unbased $H^3/H^4$ quotient and the determinant-line orientation. There is a compatible perturbation procedure as follows: prepare the finitely many reducible circle-slice obstruction maps by arbitrarily small equivariant finite-rank smoothing perturbations, and make a further generic bounded smoothing perturbation on finitely many bounded irreducible slice collars in a middle region. The procedure is fixed near the prepared reducibles and vanishes on the entire small-instanton end. The further choices may be made arbitrarily small; they form a relatively open dense transverse class on the prescribed smaller middle collars.

The resulting regular irreducible zero set is an oriented five-manifold. Its ideal completion is compact, has one small-instanton boundary stratum identified with $X$, and has exactly the finitely many prepared reducible cone points, with no other strata. A neighborhood of each cone point is a cone on $\mathbb{CP}^2$. Delete smaller open cone neighborhoods and add the small-instanton boundary. The result is a smooth compact oriented five-manifold with boundary $X$ and one projective-plane link for each actual reducible orbit, with their induced orientations. Each projective link has one of the two complex-orientation signs; no common sign or numerical spectral-flow computation is asserted. The orientation on the component with the small-instanton end can be chosen so that this boundary is $X$ with its given orientation. The number of projective links is at most $b_2(X)$.

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed simply connected oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold with positive-definite intersection form, and $E$ a Hermitian rank-two bundle with fixed unit determinant and $c_2(E)[X]=-1$. Use the equation $F_A^-=0$ and the unbased $H^3/H^4$ configuration quotient. The actual smooth reducible solution orbits are finite. Sending such a solution to its pair of parallel eigenlines gives an injection into the unordered pairs $\{x,-x\}$ in $H^2(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $x^2[X]=1$. Distinct pairs arising in this way are orthogonal, so there are at most $b_2(X)$ reducible solution orbits.

At each such orbit there are invariant Coulomb-slice coordinates with effective circle stabilizer. The finite obstruction map is a smooth circle-equivariant map $\phi:\mathbb C^{3+p}\to\mathbb C^p$, with $\phi(0)=D\phi(0)=0$ and scalar circle action of the same nonzero weight on both spaces. Arbitrarily small $C^1(H^3,H^2)$, bounded $H^3$-valued, equivariant perturbations supported near that orbit can be chosen so that their zero set near it, before taking the circle quotient, is equivariantly diffeomorphic to a neighborhood of $0$ in $\mathbb C^3$. After quotient it is a cone on $\mathbb{CP}^2$, with smooth irreducible punctured part. The finitely many constructions may have disjoint supports.

Deleting a smaller cone neighborhood leaves a smooth boundary link diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^2$. An orientation of the surrounding regular moduli manifold induces one of its two orientations; the result does not assert a common sign for distinct links. This is a local preparation operation and does not assert a small-instanton end or a global compactification.

Assume AC. Let $Y$ be a compact oriented Hausdorff topological five-manifold with supplied boundary collar, and let $X=\partial Y$ have its boundary orientation. Supply a based homomorphism $\psi:\pi_1Y\to G$ on each component, where $G$ is an arbitrary discrete group, with the standard unitary regular coefficient systems. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(X,\psi|_X)=0,\qquad \operatorname{sign}(X)=0.$$
In particular, when $X=X_1\sqcup(-X_0)$, the ordinary and $L^2$ signatures of these closed oriented four-manifolds agree across this actual coefficient-extending TOP bordism. The equality is unchanged under embedding the target group in a larger group. This theorem asserts bordism invariance and does not assert existence of a bordism between arbitrary closed coefficient manifolds.

Assume AC. For every $N\geq0$ identify
$\mathbb{CP}^N=\operatorname{Gr}_1(\mathbb C^{N+1})$, the space of complex
lines in $\mathbb C^{N+1}$, and let $\gamma$ be the tautological complex line
with $x=e(\gamma_{\mathbb R})\in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^N;\mathbb Z)$ its Euler class
in the complex orientation. Then, as a graded ring,
$$H^*(\mathbb{CP}^N;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[x]/(x^{N+1}),$$
the class $x$ generating each even degree and the odd groups vanishing; for
$0\leq m\leq N$ the standard inclusion
$\mathbb{CP}^m\hookrightarrow\mathbb{CP}^N$, induced by
$\mathbb C^{m+1}\subseteq\mathbb C^{N+1}$, pulls $x$ back to $x$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: **An actual bordism rather than an assumed end.** If $b=0$ the free intersection group has rank zero and its empty integral basis gives the claim. Suppose $b>0$. A charge-minus-one bundle exists: glue a trivial bundle on a ball to the trivial bundle on its complement by the unit-quaternion clutching function on the common three-sphere, with the sign used by the explicit BPST construction in the Taubes proof. Its smooth model connection has $c_2[X]=-1$, by the displayed curvature integral $8\pi^2$ and the fixed sign convention. Apply [F2] on this actual bundle. It gives a compact oriented smooth five-manifold $W$ whose full boundary is $X$ together with $n$ oriented projective-plane links, where $n$ is the actual number of reducible solution orbits. The determinant orientation can be chosen so the $X$ boundary has its given orientation. Closed components of $W$ have empty boundary and do not affect this assertion.

**The signed boundary inequality forces enough reducibles.** Positive definiteness makes $\operatorname{sign}(X)=b$. Each projective link has signature $\varepsilon_i\in\{1,-1\}$ by [F4]. Additivity of the intersection form under finite disjoint union and [F3] give $0=b+\sum_{i=1}^n\varepsilon_i$, hence $b\le n$. The actual reducible classification in [F2] gives $n\le b$, since its $n$ distinct unordered norm-one pairs are mutually orthogonal and nonzero. Thus $n=b$ (and the boundary equation also forces every $\varepsilon_i=-1$ for this chosen orientation). No numerical spectral-flow label or prior common sign was assumed.

**The integral basis, not merely a real diagonalization.** Choose one representative $x_i$ from each of these $b$ unordered norm-one pairs in cohomology. They satisfy $x_i\cdot x_j=\delta_{ij}$ by [F2]. Let $L=H^2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$. They are a real basis of $L\otimes\mathbb R$ because they are $b$ nonzero orthogonal vectors. For every $y\in L$, its real-basis expansion is $y=\sum_i(y\cdot x_i)x_i$. Every coefficient is an integer by integrality of [F1], so $y$ belongs to their integral span. Thus these vectors are an integral basis of the full lattice, not a proper finite-index sublattice. Integral Poincare duality identifies this lattice with the homological intersection lattice in [F1]. Transporting this basis gives the asserted identity matrix on $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$. The rank-zero case was already covered, and this proves the original diagonalization conclusion.

Assume AC. If $D\subset B^4$ is a smooth proper embedded disk, the connected double cover $W\to B^4$ branched along $D$ is a compact connected oriented smooth $4$-manifold with $H_i(W;\mathbb F_2)=0$ for $i>0$, hence $H_i(W;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $i>0$. Its boundary is the double cover of $S^3$ branched over $\partial D$.

Here a proper embedded disk means a smooth embedding of the closed disk $D^2$ whose interior lies in the interior of $B^4$ and whose boundary circle lies in $S^3=\partial B^4$; the embedding is taken neat, so it meets $S^3$ transversely along $\partial D$ and carries a boundary collar. All homology below is singular homology.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, choose its compact exterior $E_K$ with boundary torus $T_K$, and let $\mu$ and $\lambda$ be its positive meridian and preferred longitude. The exterior homology theorem gives $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$. Let $\phi:\pi_1(E_K)\to\mathbb Z$ be the composite of abelianization with the homomorphism $[\mu]\mapsto1$. For an integer $q\ge2$, let $\phi_q$ be the composite $\pi_1(E_K)\xrightarrow{\phi}\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, and let $p_q:E_q\to E_K$ be the connected cover classified by $\ker\phi_q$. On $T_K$, the homomorphism sends $[\mu]\mapsto1$ and $[\lambda]\mapsto0$, so the preimage of $T_K$ is a connected torus cover whose fundamental group corresponds to $\langle\mu^q,\lambda\rangle$. Let $\widetilde\mu$ be the closed lift of $\mu^q$. Attach a solid torus to $E_q$ with its meridian identified with $\widetilde\mu$; the resulting oriented closed $3$-manifold is the $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $\Sigma_q(K)$. In tubular coordinates near $K$, the extended map to $S^3$ has local form $(s,w)\mapsto(s,w^q)$, and the deck group $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$ acts by $w\mapsto e^{2\pi i/q}w$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold whose boundary $M$ is a rational homology three-sphere, meaning $H_*(M;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$. The boundary intersection lattice has underlying group $L_W=H_2(W;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$. Poincaré–Lefschetz duality identifies each $x\in H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$ with a class $\alpha_x\in H^2(W,M;\mathbb Z)$. Define $Q_W(\bar x,\bar y)=\langle\alpha_x\smile\alpha_y,[W,M]\rangle$, where $\smile$ is the relative cup product and $[W,M]\in H_4(W,M;\mathbb Z)$ is the relative orientation class; equivalently, this is the signed intersection number of interior two-cycle representatives. Its rank is $b_2(W)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_2(W;\mathbb Q)$. A nondegenerate positive-definite $Q_W$ is called a positive-definite filling lattice. It is not required to be unimodular; the boundary linking form can make its determinant have absolute value greater than one.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with rational-homology-sphere boundary $M$. The signed intersection pairing on interior two-cycles descends to a symmetric integer-valued bilinear form on $H_2(W;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$, this group is free of finite rank, and the form is nondegenerate after extending scalars to $\mathbb Q$. The form need not be unimodular.

Let $X=U\cup V$, where $U$ and $V$ are open path-connected subsets of $X$, let $U\cap V$ be path-connected, and fix $x_0\in U\cap V$. For the inclusion-induced maps in the diagram

$$\pi_1(U,x_0)\longleftarrow\pi_1(U\cap V,x_0)\longrightarrow\pi_1(V,x_0),$$

the group $\pi_1(X,x_0)$, together with the two inclusion-induced homomorphisms, is a pushout ([[def-pushout-of-group-homomorphisms]]). Equivalently, the canonical homomorphism from any pushout $P$ of the displayed diagram to $\pi_1(X,x_0)$ is an isomorphism. No injectivity of either map from the overlap group is assumed.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;G)\to H_n(U;G)\oplus H_n(V;G)\to H_n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(U\cap V;G)\to\cdots$$
is exact, with middle map $(u,v)\mapsto u+v$.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar.

Assume AC. For every abelian group A, A⊗_Z Q is its positive-integer localization: every element is a/s and a/s=0 iff a is killed by some positive integer. Thus A⊗Q=0 iff A is torsion. Rationalization is exact and commutes with direct sums. Naturally for every space Y, H_j(Y;Z)⊗Q≅H_j(Y;Q); for every rational vector space V, H_j(Y;V)≅H_j(Y;Q)⊗_Q V.

derivations.claim: By [F3], $D$ is a smooth proper slice disk; [F1] and [F2] then give a compact rational homology four-ball $B_D$ with boundary $M=\Sigma_2(K)$. The boundary identification in the statement permits the smooth oriented gluing $X=W\cup_M(-B_D)$; collars [F7] give a smooth closed oriented four-manifold.

Applying [F5] to the collar-thickened union gives $\pi_1(X)=\pi_1(W)*_{\pi_1(M)}\pi_1(B_D)$. Since $\pi_1(W)=1$, this pushout is the quotient of $\pi_1(B_D)$ by the normal closure of the image of $\pi_1(M)$. That normal closure is all of $\pi_1(B_D)$ by [A1], so $\pi_1(X)=1$.

In the rational Mayer–Vietoris sequence of [F6], $H_2(M;\mathbb Q)=H_1(M;\mathbb Q)=0$ and $H_i(B_D;\mathbb Q)=0$ for $i>0$ by [F1]. Thus inclusion induces an isomorphism $H_2(W;\mathbb Q)\cong H_2(X;\mathbb Q)$, so $b_2(X)=b_2(W)$. By [F8], $H_2(W;\mathbb Z)\otimes\mathbb Q\cong H_2(W;\mathbb Q)$, and the kernel of the integral-to-rational map is exactly the torsion subgroup. If an integral class maps to torsion in $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$, its rational image vanishes; the isomorphism forces its rational class in $W$ to vanish, so it was torsion. Therefore the induced map on torsion-free quotients is injective and has full rank.

Represent classes of $W$ by two-cycles in its interior and make two representatives transverse. Their signed intersection points are unchanged in the glued manifold, so the map of step 1.3 preserves the intersection form. Its rational extension is an isomorphism and transports the positive-definite form of $W$ to $X$; hence $Q_X$ is positive definite.

citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot such that its double branched cover $M=\Sigma_2(K)$ is a rational homology sphere. Let $D\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper embedded disk with boundary $K$, and let $B_D$ be the connected double cover of $B^4$ branched over $D$. Let $W$ be a compact connected smooth simply connected oriented four-manifold with boundary identified orientation-compatibly with $M$, and assume its boundary intersection form is positive definite. Assume also that the image of $\pi_1(M)\to\pi_1(B_D)$ normally generates $\pi_1(B_D)$, meaning its normal closure is the whole group. Then the oriented gluing $X=W\cup_M(-B_D)$ is a closed smooth simply connected positive-definite four-manifold, and inclusion induces an isometric full-rank embedding $Q_W\hookrightarrow Q_X$ of integral intersection lattices with $b_2(X)=b_2(W)$.

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed connected smooth simply connected oriented four-manifold. If its integral intersection form is positive definite, then there is an integral basis of $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$ in which the form is the identity matrix. Equivalently, the integral intersection lattice is isometric to the standard diagonal lattice $\mathbb Z^{b_2(X)}$ with dot product.

derivations.claim: Suppose a smooth slice disk $D$ existed. The universal assumption [A1] supplies the normal-generation hypothesis for this actual $D$, so the proved conditional gluing implication [F1] gives a closed smooth simply connected positive-definite manifold $X$ and an isometric full-rank embedding $Q_W\hookrightarrow Q_X$. Its rank is $n$ by the same gluing result. This uses the explicit hypothesis and does not infer normal generation from rational homology.

By [F2], $Q_X$ is isometric to $\mathbb Z^n$ with its dot product. Composing that isometry with the embedding in step 1.1 contradicts the assumed absence of an isometric full-rank embedding $Q_W\hookrightarrow\mathbb Z^n$. Thus no smooth slice disk exists, proving precisely the conditional nonsliceness conclusion. No larger lower bound on the smooth four-ball genus is deduced.
